subject.title: fix(codex): keep runtime context out of turn input

question: Should this PR depend on Codex `additionalContext` despite its retained, per-value-capped behavior, or should OpenClaw wait for/use a different current-turn context seam?
rationale: The correct fix depends on the maintained Codex/OpenClaw contract for large user-editable runtime context, not only on a local TypeScript patch.

options.title: Require a non-retained large-context seam
options.body: Keep the PR blocked until runtime context is delivered through a path that does not replay old per-turn values and can preserve OpenClaw's large context budget.

options.title: Accept the additionalContext tradeoff
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally accept Codex's retention and truncation semantics, but that should be explicit and backed by user-visible multi-turn proof.

options.title: Pause this branch
options.body: Pause or close this PR if the needed contract must first be designed upstream in Codex.

recommendation.title: Require a non-retained large-context seam
recommendation.body: Keep the PR blocked until runtime context is delivered through a path that does not replay old per-turn values and can preserve OpenClaw's large context budget.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows broad ownership of Codex app-server run-attempt and thread-routing boundaries that would need to absorb this contract decision.
